identity.title: Oncogenic histone hyperacetylation drives acute myeloid leukemia through enforced transcription initiation of leukemogenic genes.

content.abstract: Histone acetylation is tightly correlated with active transcription, yet its causal roles and downstream mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Chromosomal translocations generating fusion proteins involving histone acetyltransferases (HATs) represent a powerful but underexplored system to dissect how dysregulated acetylation rewires transcriptional control. Here, we establish an endogenous mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) driven by a fusion between two HATs, KAT6A and p300, generated through CRISPR-mediated chromosomal rearrangement. KAT6A-p300 induces aggressive, transplantable AML and confers oncogene addiction. Mechanistically, the fusion establishes broad promoter-associated hyperacetylated domains. This hyperacetylation promotes recruitment and remodeling by the canonical BAF complex, increasing promoter accessibility and stimulating RNA polymerase II recruitment and transcription initiation. Fusion formation also redistributes wild-type p300, broadens its chromatin occupancy, and stabilizes its association with fusion-bound loci. Together, our findings establish histone hyperacetylation as a driver of transcription and reveal a direct mechanistic link between aberrant acetylation, chromatin remodeling, and leukemogenesis.
